questionText: Ali's parents have not bought ...... of the two recommended books.
explanation: When referring to a choice between two items in a negative sentence, 'either' is the correct pronoun/determiner to use with 'not'[cite: 72, 74].

questionText: We were served a ....... meal at that cosy restaurant.
explanation: Adjective order in English generally follows opinion (delicious), physical quality/attribute (spicy), and origin (Spanish)[cite: 72, 74].

questionText: Last Wednesday, it rained heavily ...... the match was played.
explanation: The conjunction 'yet' (or 'still/nevertheless') is used to express contrast between heavy rain and the fact that the match was still played[cite: 72, 74].

questionText: Adwoa's daughter is allergic ....... dust.
explanation: The adjective 'allergic' is followed by the preposition 'to'[cite: 72, 74].

questionText: Konlaan suggested that it was time they ....... for the meeting.
explanation: The expression 'it is time' (or 'it was time') is followed by a verb in the past subjunctive tense ('left')[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: At my last interview, I faced ....... panel.
explanation: Compound adjectives used before nouns take a singular hyphenated form ('a seven-member panel')[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: Last month, there was ...... eclipse of the sun.
explanation: Unique celestial events take specific modifiers, phrased as 'an eclipse of the sun'[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: Dauda saw the thief ...... out of the shop.
explanation: Verbs of perception (like see, hear, watch) take the bare infinitive or present participle when witnessing an action ('saw the thief run')[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: If Azameti had won gold, Ghanaians .......
explanation: Third conditional sentences ('If + past perfect') require 'would have + past participle' in the main clause[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: Among the participants for the competition, Eugenia got here ....... early.
explanation: 'Very' is an intensifier used before an adverb or adjective ('very early')[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: Afiba's aunt, ....... lives in Tamale spoke to us very courteously.
explanation: 'Who' is the subjective relative pronoun used to refer to a person (Afiaba's aunt) performing the action of the relative clause[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: You haven't met each other before, ....... you?
explanation: A negative statement ('haven't met') takes a positive auxiliary verb in the question tag ('have you')[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: Which of the ....... fragrance(s) is milder?
explanation: The comparative adjective 'milder' compares a choice between two items ('Which of the two fragrances')[cite: 72, 75].

questionText: For winning the first position in the Essay Competition, the school gave Linda a laptop. (Passive form: Linda ....... given a laptop by the school.)
explanation: The active sentence is in the simple past tense ('gave'), so the passive equivalent requires the past tense 'was'[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: Reported speech for: "I will keep my word", promised Kende.
options: Kende promise to keep her word.
Kende promised to keep her word.
Kende is promising to keep her word.
Kende promises to keep her word.
explanation: The reporting verb is past tense ('promised'), requiring backshifting of tenses and pronoun adjustment ('promised to keep her word')[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: Mama said, "You can only fight off bullies if you are assertive". (Nearest in meaning to 'assertive')
explanation: 'Assertive' means confident, forceful, and bold in expressing oneself[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: The salient points of the topic have been thoroughly discussed. (Nearest in meaning to 'salient')
explanation: 'Salient' points refer to the most notable, chief, or important points[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: Little Asabea wondered why her grandfather walked so slowly. (Nearest in meaning to 'wondered')
explanation: To wonder about something is to be curious about why or how it happens[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: The rampant destruction of property must be checked. (Nearest in meaning to 'rampant')
explanation: 'Rampant' means flourishing or spreading unchecked and uncontrolled[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: We're so excited because Amuzu's proposal has been accepted. (Nearest in meaning to 'proposal')
explanation: A proposal is a formal plan or suggestion put forward for consideration[cite: 72, 76].

questionText: "Do not be such a wet blanket, Afua..." (Meaning of the underlined idiom 'wet blanket')
explanation: A 'wet blanket' is someone who dampens enthusiasm or likes to discourage others[cite: 72, 77].

questionText: The chief advised his subjects not to allow anger to get the better of them. (Meaning of 'get the better of')
explanation: To get the better of someone means to defeat, overcome, or control them[cite: 72, 77].

questionText: Asuo had to eat his words when Asante Kotoko lost... (Meaning of 'eat his words')
explanation: To 'eat one's words' means to retract a statement and admit that one was wrong[cite: 72, 77].

questionText: The fraudster was paid back in his own coins. (Meaning of 'paid back in his own coins')
explanation: To be 'paid back in one's own coin' means to be treated the same way one has treated others (in this context, swindled/cheated)[cite: 72, 77].

questionText: Yaaba hit the nail on the head when she told us... (Meaning of 'hit the nail on the head')
explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' means to find the exact truth or state something precisely right[cite: 72, 77].

questionText: Regions with abundant rainfall are different from those having ...... moisture. (Opposite of abundant)
explanation: 'Scanty' (scarce/insufficient) is the antonym of 'abundant' (plentiful)[cite: 72, 77].

questionText: Due to ongoing road construction, our shops have been temporarily closed down. (Opposite of temporarily)
explanation: 'Permanently' is the direct opposite of 'temporarily'[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: It is hard to tell when this will start or where it will ...... (Opposite of start/begin - contextually 'cease')
explanation: 'Cease' (stop/end) is opposite in meaning to begin or start[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Some exercises may seem easy in theoretical terms but can be really difficult in ....... aspects. (Opposite of theoretical)
explanation: 'Practical' is the antonym of 'theoretical'[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: It is good to get a cure for a disease, but it is better to ....... the disease. (Opposite of cure)
explanation: In medical and general health contexts, 'preventing' a disease contrasts with 'curing' it after occurrence[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Cloze test: After checking the -31- list, he realised that his name had been wrongly spelt.
explanation: An 'attendance list' or attendance sheet is checked for names at meetings[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Cloze test: Two -32- were proposed and voted on.
explanation: In formal meetings, members propose and vote on 'motions'[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Cloze test: ...ask a member to -33- for the closure of the meeting.
explanation: To 'move' for closure or adjournment is standard parliamentary procedure[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Cloze test: Tetteh Oko did and he was -34- by Adjoa Mansa.
explanation: A motion proposed ('moved') by one member is 'seconded' by another[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Cloze test: The meeting was then -35- to a new date.
explanation: Meetings are formally 'adjourned' to a future date[cite: 72, 78].

questionText: Choose the word with the same consonant sound as the underlined in: Those two are arch rivals. (arch /tʃ/)
explanation: 'Patch' contains the voiceless postalveolar affricate /tʃ/ sound as in 'arch'[cite: 72, 79].

questionText: Choose the word with the same consonant sound as the underlined in: Prosper is the new chef. (chef /ʃ/)
explanation: 'Shield' features the /ʃ/ sound, matching the initial sound in 'chef'[cite: 72, 79].

questionText: Choose the word with the same consonant sound as the underlined in: Lariba sprang to her feet. (sprang /spr/ cluster)
explanation: 'Sprayed' shares the initial consonant cluster /spr/[cite: 72, 79].

questionText: Choose the word with the same vowel sound as the underlined in: Whole grains are healthier than polished ones. (Whole /oʊ/)
explanation: 'Goal' shares the same diphthong vowel sound /oʊ/ as 'Whole'[cite: 72, 79].

questionText: Choose the word with the same vowel sound as the underlined in: The heir to the British throne... (heir /ɛə/)
explanation: 'Air' is a homophone of 'heir', sharing the identical vowel sound /ɛə/[cite: 72, 79].
